correctness.rationale: Exact canonical-form argument reduces every full-rank Hamming parity-check presentation to coordinate-basis rows plus dependent functionals. Four explicit nonzero columns induce a chordless four-cycle for r>=4. The standard-library verifier exhaustively checks all 31 single augmentations for r=5 and all 63 singles/1953 distinct pairs for r=6 by exact parity adjacency and MCS plus perfect-elimination verification, not sampling. Induced-subgraph closure lifts finite exclusions to all larger r. Pairwise-check grouped-coordinate constructions give chordal witnesses at r=3,4,5,6. The actual checker returned VERIFY_OK. Ranges: exact r=3..6; lower bounds r>=4,5,6 respectively.

value.rationale: A natural efficiency question for the new chordal decoding paradigm is the extra parity-check equation overhead needed to make a fixed classical code graph chordal. Hamming codes are canonical perfect distance-three codes. This theorem identifies the first nonchordal redundancy, sharp repair costs at three successive redundancies, and induced-subgraph lower bounds that remain true for every larger Hamming code. The exact invariant is not an arbitrary code instance, and the finite checks enumerate all row-space-equivalent presentations in each target dimension.
